newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Data dearth dulls Bund volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Data dearth dulls Bund volatility.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE started to slide on Monday, and traders said this was likely to continue in later trade as there was little data to inspire activity.
Renewed grumblings over a single European currency during the weekend had washed over the market, but left it largely unruffled, said a trader at a U.S. brokerage.

German "wise man" government economic adviser Juergen Donges was quoted in a Spanish newspaper as saying a pact between Germany and France to delay the planned 1999 start to European economic and monetary union (EMU) could not be ruled out.
"We're not seeing any sharp moves, but expect a steady erosion," said a British bank broker. "Volatility can go cheaper."

There were no major data due in the U.S. until Tuesday's employment cost index, and traders said that, combined with the prospect of the key non-farm payrolls data on Friday, would prevent volatility from falling too low.
"There are buyers hovering around the five-and-a-quarter level," said the British bank broker.

September Bund volatility was at 5.39 percent, compared with 5.5 percent on Friday. October options on the December future were off 0.10 percent at 5.28 percent, and November was fractionally higher at 5.26 percent.

December volatility was steady to slightly lower at 5.42 percent. September Bund futures were down 0.17 at 102.74, while December was down 0.16 at 101.89. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
